title: Customer-specific prompt-set ingestion and online A/B routing for rerank evals
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reproducible pipeline and online hooks to evaluate reranking model changes per-customer using ingestible customer prompt sets. Goals: (1) accept customer-provided prompt sets and canonicalize them into our eval format, (2) run batched offline NDCG/MRR scoring against baseline and candidate rerankers, (3) provide online A/B routing and telemetry so we can measure real-world delta with controlled traffic, and (4) enforce latency budgets and scalable scoring for production rerank endpoints.
motivation: Customers have asked to see rerank quality improvements on their own prompts. Current evals are siloed and use generic datasets; we need a workflow that ties customer prompt sets to offline metrics (NDCG/MRR) and to online A/B experiments while preserving privacy and predictable latency.
acceptance_criteria: Customer prompt-set ingestion API (CSV/JSON) available and documented in Console/Docs
Offline eval pipeline computes NDCG@1/3/5/10 and MRR and stores results in eval DB
A/B routing hook can route customer traffic at configurable percentages to candidate reranker
Online telemetry surfaces per-customer NDCG and MRR proxies and click/engagement metrics in Grafana dashboard
Rerank endpoint P95 latency for 1-5 candidates remains <= 120ms in default mode
Scalable scoring path supports 2000 QPS for small candidate sets with autoscaling policy
Data retention and privacy checklist completed for customer prompt ingestion (KMS + redaction)
Integration tests for offline vs online metric correlation (sanity checks) in CI
design_decisions: Ingested customer prompt sets are canonicalized to internal EvalRecord schema and stored encrypted in eval-bucket with KMS keys per-customer
Offline evals run on the eval cluster using batched scoring worker (Ray-based prototype replaced by dedicated scoring service) to ensure consistent kernels
Use sharded synchronous scorer for low-latency paths and an async batch scorer for large-scale backfills; scheduler decides based on candidate count and latency SLO
A/B routing implemented as a lightweight policy in API gateway with traffic mirror and percentage split; flags stored in Config Service and surfaced in Console
Metric computation: use existing ndcg/mrr implementation from eval-harness but add per-customer weighting and per-prompt-type breakdown (e.g., short vs long)

metrics_targets: Offline: NDCG@10 delta >= +1.5% relative to baseline for customer prompt sets (stat sig at p<0.05)
Offline: MRR change reported with 95% CI and minimum sample size calculation
Online: Observed proxy NDCG/MRR correlation with offline >= 0.7 for initial customers
Latency: P95 <= 120ms for default scoring path (1-5 candidates)
Scale: support 2000 QPS with P95 <= 200ms using autoscaling sharded scorers
risks_mitigation: Risk: Customer prompt sets may contain PII - Mitigation: redaction rules + KMS + opt-in ingestion
Risk: Offline metrics do not correlate with online behavior - Mitigation: small-scale A/B tests and click-proxy telemetry before large rollouts
Risk: Added instrumentation increases latency - Mitigation: lightweight telemetry via sampling and off-path aggregation
Risk: Resource contention on scoring cluster - Mitigation: autoscaling policies, burst queues, and capacity reservations for dedicated customers
notes: Next major milestone: complete A/B tooling that ties Config Service flags to Console UI and roll out to 3 pilot customers. Plan: run 2-week pilot per customer, measure offline->online correlation, then enable automated rollout policy if candidate meets NDCG/MRR thresholds.
